Working notes — ticket routing

- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.
- C (regional office) rejected on 9/9 attempts: refunds, shipments, invoices across south/east/north, small/large, various senders and urgency phrases. Do not choose C for refund, shipment, or invoice requests. Mentions of “regional office” in subject/body do not make C valid.
- One accepted: REQ-2404, large claim, north region, from Client Services, body “came in through the regional office” → B priority desk accepted (+1.00).
- A standard queue has not been tried or accepted yet. No clear evidence that sender role, region, size, or urgency alone determines routing.
- Tentative rule: for claim requests, especially large/north/Client Services, prefer B. For refund/shipment/invoice requests, C is invalid; choose A or B, but no positive evidence yet. If similar large claim appears, use B. If invoice/shipment/refund appears, avoid C; consider A unless claim/large priority precedent applies.
- Open questions: Does B work for all claims? Should large invoices/shipments go B or A? Does sender role matter? Need test A vs B when C is not viable.

Working notes — ticket routing

Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Routing rules from evidence:
- C remains invalid. It has been rejected for refunds, shipments, and invoices; mentions of “regional office” in subject/body do not validate C.
- Shipment requests: use A. A accepted 3/3 for east-region shipments (REQ-2410 small, REQ-2417 small, REQ-2419 large; varied senders). No shipment B/C evidence.
- Claim requests: use B. B accepted for large north claims (REQ-2414 Client Services; REQ-2415 Regional Ops, with “regional office” mention). A rejected for small north claim (REQ-2412), so A is not valid for claims.
- Invoice requests: do not use A. A rejected for small east, small north, large north invoices (REQ-2411, 2413, 2418). C is invalid. By elimination, B is likely valid; needs direct confirmation.
- Refund requests: do not use A or C. A rejected for large south refund (REQ-2416); C invalid. By elimination, B is likely valid; needs direct confirmation.

Sender role, region, size, urgency, and wording (“no rush,” “second attempt,” scanned paperwork) have not been shown to override request type. Large north claims are B, but claim type itself appears decisive.

Tentative decision:
Shipment → A.
Claim → B.
Invoice → B.
Refund → B.
Never C.

Open questions:
- Confirm B for invoices/refunds and non-north/small claims.
- Confirm A for non-east shipments.
- Check whether any request type has valid C under untested conditions.

Working notes — ticket routing

Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Updated rules:
- C invalid for refunds, shipments, invoices; “regional office” wording does not validate C. C not yet ruled out for claims.
- Shipments: East → A (accepted small/large, varied senders). South large → not A (REQ-2426, 2429); with C invalid, B likely by elimination. North/west untested.
- Claims: North → B (large north accepted: REQ-2414, 2415, 2421). B rejected for small east (REQ-2425, 2428) and large south (REQ-2427). A rejected for small north (REQ-2412). So claim routing is region-dependent; East/South claims likely C, pending confirmation.
- Invoices: do not use A (rejected small east/north, large north). C invalid. B likely valid; needs direct confirmation.
- Refunds: B (accepted south small: REQ-2420, 2423). A/C invalid.
- Sender role, size, urgency, and wording (“no rush,” “second attempt,” scanned paperwork) still do not override request type/region.

Tentative decision:
Shipment East → A.
Shipment South/non-east → B (confirm).
Claim North → B.
Claim East/South → C? (confirm; B invalid).
Invoice → B (confirm).
Refund → B.
Never C only for refunds/shipments/invoices, not yet for claims.

Open questions:
- Confirm B for south/non-east shipments.
- Confirm C for east/south claims; test north small claim.
- Confirm B for invoices and non-south refunds.
- Test C for claims under untested conditions; previous “never C” was too broad.

Working notes — ticket routing

Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Core: request type + region matter. Size, sender role, urgency, and wording (“regional office,” “no rush,” scanned paperwork) do not override. “Regional office” wording does not validate C.

C invalid for refunds, shipments, invoices. C also rejected for small claims East/South (REQ-2432, 2436); still possible for other claims.

Shipments:
- East → A confirmed (small/large).
- B rejected for North large (REQ-2430, 2434, 2439) and South small (REQ-2435, 2437, 2438). South large not A. Prior “South/non-east → B” is wrong. Need test A for North/South shipments; C invalid.

Claims:
- North large → B (REQ-2414, 2415, 2421).
- B invalid: small East, large South. C invalid: small East/South. A invalid: small North.
- East/South claims not C; test A. North small claim untested.

Invoices:
- A invalid East/North; C invalid. B rejected South small (REQ-2433), so B not universal. Test A for South invoices; East/North unresolved.

Refunds:
- South small → B (REQ-2420, 2423). North large B rejected (REQ-2431), so B not universal. C invalid. Test A for North/non-South refunds.

Tentative:
Shipment East → A. Shipment North/South → test A (not B).
Claim North large → B. Claim East/South → test A (not B/C).
Invoice South → test A. East/North unresolved.
Refund South small → B. North/non-South → test A.

Open:
- Confirm A for North/South shipments.
- Test A for East/South claims and North small claims.
- Resolve invoices: test A South; find East/North valid route.
- Test A for North/non-South refunds.
- C remains invalid for refunds/shipments/invoices; for claims, C only ruled out East/South small.

Working notes — ticket routing

Core: request type + region. Size, sender role, urgency, wording do not.

Claims:
- East small/large → A confirmed (REQ-2440-2442, 2448). B/C invalid East small.
- North large → B. North small A untested.
- South small: A rejected (2443); C invalid; B likely—confirm.
- South large: B invalid; C/A unresolved.

Shipments:
- East → A confirmed.
- North large: A rejected (2444, 2447); B previously rejected; C previously called invalid. Contradiction: no known valid route. Re-test C/B; C may not be universally invalid for shipments.
- South small: A rejected (2445, 2446); B previously rejected; same contradiction.
- South large: not A; test B/C.

Invoices:
- A invalid East/North; C invalid; B rejected South small. Test A South; East/North unresolved.

Refunds:
- South small → B (2420, 2423).
- North large: A rejected (2449); B previously rejected; C called invalid. Contradiction. Re-test C/B; C may not be universal invalid.
- Non-South/north unresolved.

Tentative:
East claim → A. North large claim → B. South small claim → B? East shipment → A.
North/South shipments and North large refund need C re-test due contradictions.

Open:
- Confirm South small claim B; test North small claim A.
- Resolve shipment North large/South small; South large.
- Resolve invoices South/East/North; refund North/non-South.
- C: only firmly ruled out for invoices and some claims East/South small; not reliable as global invalidity.

Working notes — ticket routing

Core: request type + region only. Size, sender role, urgency, wording irrelevant (REQ-2450–2455).

Claims:
- East → A (small/large: 2440–2442, 2448, 2450–2452).
- North large → B. North small: test A.
- South small: A rejected (2443); C invalid; B likely—confirm.
- South large: B invalid; C/A unresolved.

Shipments:
- East → A.
- South → C (small 2453–2454; large 2455 confirmed).
- North small: C rejected (2458). North large: A rejected (2444, 2447); B rejected; C not globally invalid—re-test C.
- South large resolved as C.

Invoices:
- A invalid East/North and South large (2457, 2459). C invalid. B rejected South small. South: test B/C.

Refunds:
- South small → B (2420, 2423).
- East large: B rejected (2456). Test A/C.
- North large: A rejected (2449); B rejected; C called invalid—re-test C.

Tentative:
East claim → A. North large claim → B. South small claim → B? East shipment → A. South shipment → C.

Open:
- Confirm South small claim B; test North small claim A.
- Resolve North large shipment; North large refund; invoices South (B/C); refund East (A/C); non-South/north refunds.
- C: invalid for invoices and North small shipment; valid for South shipments; not globally invalid.

Working notes — ticket routing

Core: route by request type + region only. Size, sender role, urgency, wording irrelevant.

Claims:
- East → A.
- North large → B. North small: test A/B.
- South small: A rejected; C invalid; B likely. South large: B invalid; C/A unresolved.

Shipments:
- East → A.
- South → C (small/large confirmed).
- North small: C rejected; A/B unresolved.
- North large: A/B rejected; C not globally invalid—re-test C.

Invoices:
- A invalid East/North and South large. B invalid South (small and large 2466).
- C invalid for some invoices; not globally invalid. South invoice unresolved: A/B invalid, test C.

Refunds:
- South small → B (2420, 2423).
- North small → B (2461); C rejected (2462).
- East: A invalid (2460, 2464, 2467–2469). B invalid East large (2456); size irrelevant, so East refund likely C. Confirm.
- North large: A/B rejected; C called invalid—re-test C.

Tentative:
East claim → A. North large claim → B. North small refund → B. South small refund → B. East refund → C? East shipment → A. South shipment → C. South invoice → C?

Open:
- Confirm East refund C.
- North small shipment A/B; North large shipment C; North large refund C.
- South invoice C/other; South small claim B; North small claim A/B.
- C status: invalid for invoices? and North small shipment; valid for South shipments; not globally invalid.
